why: Questions whose only target concept was retired when the course was cut back to the concepts ARENA actually uses. Ids are POSITIONAL in the CSV sources, so retiring by id here is the only safe way to drop a drill: deleting the CSV row would renumber every question after it and silently re-point every qmatrix tag and every stored served_question_id. Nothing is deleted -- the rows stay in the CSVs and the pages stay in This-Directory-Only/archive/, so restoring a concept is removing its ids from this list.

split_kcs.why: Concepts whose PAGE is archived because the concept was SPLIT into narrower ones, not because it left the course. The id is gone from kc_registry.json and its page is filed in the archive beside the retired ones, so the archive watcher must know about it — but none of its drills were retired and nothing it taught was dropped.

kcs.numpy.random-generator: 2026-08-31 -> numpy.random-samplers + numpy.random-threading + numpy.random-seeding. It declared ten symbols behind one mastery number and drilled five of them across three questions; see This-Directory-Only/SPEC_NODE_SPLITTING.md.

also_retired_with_their_prerequisite.why: Drills on a SURVIVING concept whose solution reached for a symbol only a retired page taught. The prerequisite guard found them; each is retired rather than rewritten because the symbol itself is what ARENA does not use.

ids.5: torch.linalg.norm (0 ARENA notebooks) — its whole 'norms' segment went with it
ids.130: torch.where, taught only by the retired where-select page
ids.386: Tensor.flip, taught only by the retired argsort-ranking page
ids.393: torch.repeat_interleave (0), taught only by the retired tile-repeat-meshgrid page

kept_back_to_keep_an_atom_trainable.why: These two drills were the ONLY questions training a BKT atom that gates other questions, so retiring them would have locked their dependents for every learner (pipeline/audit_question_bank.py --gate, atom_prereq_untrainable). Both are re-homed onto a concept that survives and honestly owns them.

ids.103: softmax-from-logits -> numpy.axis-reductions (exp, max, sum over an axis)
